text.p: Tropical Cyclone Harold, with 45 mph winds, is in the Coral Sea, east of Queensland, Australia, near 17s/155e, moving southwest at 8 mph. Harold is expected to continue its track while slowly intensifying. It will still be well off the coast of Queensland by 48 hours, threatening only shipping. It is at least a few days away from Queensland.

Tropical Cyclone Karlette, with 45 mph winds, is in the Indian Ocean near 15s/77e, moving west at 7 mph. A turn to the west southwest is likely this period as Karlette slowly intensifies. Karlette is only a threat to shipping at this time.

Storms continue to be very strong in the northeastern Atlantic, spreading areas of strong westerly winds across northwestern Europe. This is again expected during the next few days through midweek. High seas cause problems for shipping in the North Sea and English Channel.
